query: Consider the following context: The recent perspective of multiprincipal element alloys (MPEAs), also known as high-entropy alloys (HEAs), has emerged as a very promising area for material design. Additive manufacturing (AM) strategies have also been noted to provide additional strength to HEA systems. In the selected dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA system, an additional strength of approximately 300–400 MPa was achieved by adopting an additive manufacturing route as compared to its cast and wrought counterparts. However, the challenge of oxidation degradation always imposes a severe limitation for high-temperature applications in gas turbines, power plants, and aerospace components. Hence, ensuring material sustainability, longevity, and integrity for high-temperature applications inevitably requires the exploration of the oxidation behavior of alloys. In that context, which method can be used for elucidating the mechanistic aspects and elemental redistribution of nanoprecipitates on oxidation behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Atom Probe Tomography (APT) can be used to elucidate the mechanistic aspects and elemental redistribution of nanoprecipitates during high‐temperature oxidation of the dual‐nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy because its near-atomic resolution enables sensitive compositional profiling at the precipitate–matrix interfaces where oxidation-driven segregation occurs.
generation.material_initial_state: Dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy produced via additive manufacturing, featuring two distinct types of nanoprecipitates embedded in a predominantly BCC matrix.
generation.intervention: Exposure of the alloy to controlled high-temperature oxidation environments (e.g., 800–1000 °C in air) for defined durations.
generation.conditions: High-temperature oxidation tests under controlled atmospheres (with defined oxygen partial pressures) that mimic service conditions in gas turbines, power plants, and aerospace components.
generation.structural_mediator: The nanoprecipitates and their interfaces with the surrounding matrix, which mediate how elemental redistribution occurs during oxidation.
generation.mechanism: During high-temperature oxidation, differential diffusion and oxidation kinetics lead to segregation of specific elements (e.g., Cr or Ti) at the nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces, altering local phase stability and oxide formation. APT can capture these gradients at the atomic scale, revealing the underlying mechanistic pathways.
generation.predicted_outcome: APT analysis will reveal significant elemental segregation at the nanoprecipitate boundaries in oxidized samples relative to unoxidized ones, indicating that changes in local chemistry are responsible for forming protective or less-protective oxide phases.
generation.baseline: Standard oxidation characterization relying on bulk techniques (e.g., thermogravimetric analysis and conventional TEM/EDS mapping) that do not resolve atomic-scale compositional gradients in nanoprecipitates.
generation.boundary: The approach may be limited by challenges in preparing representative APT specimens from oxidized materials and potential beam-induced artifacts; also, the quantification of light elements may introduce uncertainties.
generation.uncertainty: While APT is expected to resolve compositional modifications at the nanoscale, uncertainties remain regarding the precise correlation between observed segregation profiles and overall oxidation rates, especially under varying temperature and exposure times.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a set of identical dual-nanoprecipitation high-entropy alloy samples and subject half to high-temperature oxidation (e.g., 900 °C for several hours) while keeping the other half as unoxidized controls. Using focused ion beam (FIB) milling, extract needle-shaped specimens from regions near the nanoprecipitates in both groups and perform APT analysis to obtain atomic-scale compositional profiles. Complement the APT findings with TEM-EDS mapping of the same regions.
measurements: Atomic-scale compositional maps of nanoprecipitates and surrounding matrix
Quantification of segregation levels of key elements (e.g., Cr, Ti) at precipitate–matrix interfaces
Oxide layer thickness and phase identification via TEM
Bulk oxidation kinetics via thermogravimetric analysis (TGA)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If APT studies do not demonstrate distinguishing elemental segregation or if the compositional profiles in oxidized regions are statistically indistinguishable from those in unoxidized samples, then the hypothesis that APT can elucidate the oxidation-induced elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitates is falsified.

Question: How does the molten salt corrosion behavior of the dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy compare to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 in a NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 environment at temperatures relevant to concentrating solar power systems?. System: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) and duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205). Processing: Vacuum-arc-melting of high purity constituent elements (99.95 wt.% purity) with multiple re-melts for homogeneity; samples cut to 20 mm × 5 mm × 2 mm, polished to 1200-grit, degreased with acetone, and dried; corrosion tests performed in a custom tube furnace with 20 mm salt melt depth at 450 °C and 650 °C for 24 h.
